status_reasoning: Reviewers explicitly affirm that 'the compound is remarkably potent, hitting its unknown target(s) when applied to cells at a submicromolar concentration' and describe ISRIB as acting 'as a potent and stereospecific inhibitor with an IC50 of 5 nM.' The potency and stereospecificity of ISRIB are accepted without challenge.

Reviewers acknowledge that 'the functional characterisation of the compound is rather thorough' and accept that ISRIB specifically blocks PERK signaling without affecting other UPR branches. These claims about ISRIB's selectivity and mechanism are not questioned.

Reviewers state that 'the functional characterization of the compound is rather thorough and thus its utility as a tool compound is well documented.' The claims about ISRIB reversing translational attenuation and acting downstream of all eIF2α kinases are accepted as part of this thorough functional characterization.

Reviewers explicitly note that 'the functional characterisation of ISRIB is very thorough, it is not matched by a similar level of molecular detail. We do not know if ISRIB directly modulates the interaction of eIF2α with eIF2B or the competing interactions with eIF5 or some aspect of eIF2B activity.' They request co-immunoprecipitation experiments to clarify the mechanism, indicating uncertainty about the molecular target.

Reviewers request additional evidence, stating 'it was deemed important to assess the likelihood that ISRIB affects memory formation by acting on brain cells, as opposed to eliciting these effects by peripheral action' and ask to 'determine if the compound gets into the CNS, when applied at doses that affect memory.' While pharmacokinetic data are presented, reviewers want functional confirmation of CNS activity.

Reviewers state they 'were impressed by effects on memory formation, which is enhanced by application of the compound,' showing general support. However, they raise a methodological concern: 'ISRIB treatment was post-training for water maze and cued fear conditioning...but ISRIB treatment was chronic prior to training for contextual fear conditioning' and ask authors to 'address how this affects the conclusions regarding the compounds impact on memory consolidation.' This inconsistency creates uncertainty about the interpretation.

The claims about ISRIB sensitizing cells to ER stress and synergizing with stress to induce apoptosis are part of the functional characterization that reviewers describe as 'rather thorough.' These findings are not questioned or challenged in the review.

Reviewers explicitly affirm the novelty, stating 'No one has previously reported a functionally similar inhibitor–in fact, until this report, it was unsuspected that this node in the ISR was even susceptible to inhibition.' This strongly supports the claim that ISRIB is the first reported ISR antagonist.

Reviewers express optimism about ISRIB's utility, stating 'there is reason to hope that ISRIB will be applied to much further research and that this paper will serve as a foundation for such studies.' This supports the speculative claims about ISRIB's potential as a research tool and therapeutic agent.
